and that is all I really think of him as a player in the NFL...

It is always a struggle for me to find that happy medium: What level of interest/information should we have in a players off-field life. Do we (or indeed, should we) care about Tiger woods banging every waitress in sight if he can still nail his short game as well? Do wee need to know every time Ritchie Incognito goes after his Ferrari with a hammer? Where do I/we/you draw the line? Should wife-beating & dog strangling keep people off the field? What about when outside life does appear on the field (Tebowing)?

I personally don't want to watch inhuman, passionless robots on the field (though I know that encourages gold cleats, sharpie pockets in socks and after TD dancing). But I also feel that these players have a lot of attention on them off the field and they are role models whether we like it or not. Does the league need a stringent off-field behavior policy? (with the money these guys make I don't see that actually being effective)
